finding: The PyTorch tensor backend implements only Vehicle A planar3. Vehicles B and C use coupled6, so long-horizon Node-to-tensor parity for coupled6 cannot currently be measured.

figure_impact.Fig 3: GPU/tensor claims are restricted to Vehicle A planar3 until this work package passes.
figure_impact.Fig 6: All three vehicles can run affordably through the authoritative persistent Node bridge, but this is a different backend from a tensor-only Fig 3.
figure_impact.cross_figure_risk: Backend scope must be printed directly in captions; otherwise the paper would imply unsupported three-vehicle GPU coverage.

implementation_scope: Batched coupled6 rigid-body state and RK4 integration
Full mass/added-mass, Coriolis, damping, hydrostatics, wind/current/wave force ordering parity
Vehicle B propeller/rudder internal state and Vehicle C dual-azimuth actuator/allocation state
Checkpoint schema v3 including filters, integrator, allocator and RNG state
Float64 CPU reference parity for 2400 steps before any CUDA path
Float32 CUDA determinism and divergence characterization only after CPU acceptance

estimate.engineering: large; approximately 2-4 focused engineer-weeks plus validation, not a wrapper change
estimate.paper_deadline_decision: Decision taken: Fig 3 and every GPU/tensor claim are limited to Vehicle A planar3. Fig 6 uses the authoritative Node bridge and makes no GPU claim. A figure guard enforces this boundary.

current_affordability.interpretation: Approximately 6.3 minutes of simulator stepping before training and evaluation overhead; the Node path makes the three-vehicle transfer matrix computationally plausible today.
